title: Λύκοι καὶ πρόβατα
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 217. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λύκοι ἐπιβουλεύοντες ποίμνῃ προβάτων, ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἠδύναντο αὐτῶν περιγενέσθαι διὰ τοὺς φυλάττοντας αὐτὰ κύνας, ἔγνωσαν δεῖν διὰ δόλου τοῦτο πρᾶξαι.
sentences.tr: Lykoi epibouleuontes poimnēi probatōn, epeidē ouk ēdynanto autōn perigenesthai dia tous phylattontas auta kynas, egnōsan dein dia dolou touto praxai.
sentences.l: Wolves plotting against a flock of sheep, since they were not able to get-the-better-of them because of the dogs guarding them, judged that it was necessary to accomplish this by guile.
sentences.i: Some wolves had designs on a flock of sheep, but could not overpower them because of the dogs that guarded them; so they judged that the thing would have to be done by a trick.
sentences.n: περιγίνομαι takes the genitive of the party one gets the better of. ἔγνωσαν δεῖν is the aorist of γιγνώσκω in its deciding sense, 'came to the judgment that it was necessary', with the infinitive πρᾶξαι under δεῖν. αὐτά, the object of φυλάττοντας, is neuter and so points back to πρόβατα: the dogs guard the sheep.

sentences.t: Καὶ πέμψαντες πρέσβεις ἐξῄτουν παρ’ αὐτῶν τοὺς κύνας, λέγοντες ὡς ἐκεῖνοι τῆς ἔχθρας αἴτιοί εἰσιν, καί, εἰ ἐγχειρίσουσιν αὐτούς, εἰρήνη μεταξὺ αὐτῶν γενήσεται.
sentences.tr: Kai pempsantes presbeis exēitoun par’ autōn tous kynas, legontes hōs ekeinoi tēs echthras aitioi eisin, kai, ei encheirisousin autous, eirēnē metaxy autōn genēsetai.
sentences.l: And having sent envoys, they kept demanding the dogs from them, saying that those were the cause of the enmity, and that, if they would hand them over, peace would come to be between them.
sentences.i: So they sent envoys and demanded the dogs of them, saying that the dogs were the cause of the hostility, and that if they were handed over there would be peace between the two sides.
sentences.n: ὡς after a verb of saying introduces reported speech, and Greek keeps the tenses of the words actually spoken — εἰσιν present, γενήσεται future — where English shifts them back. The subject of ἐγχειρίσουσιν is the sheep, who are being asked to do the handing over. ἐγχειρίζω is to put a thing into another's hands, to hand over. The vocabulary throughout is diplomatic: πρέσβεις, ἔχθρα, εἰρήνη, which is what makes the moral about cities fit.

sentences.t: Τὰ δὲ πρόβατα μὴ προϊδόμενα τὸ μέλλον ἐξέδωκαν αὐτούς, καὶ οἱ λύκοι περιγενόμενοι ἐκείνων ῥᾳδίως καὶ τὴν ποίμνην ἀφύλακτον οὖσαν διέφθειραν.
sentences.tr: Ta de probata mē proidomena to mellon exedōkan autous, kai hoi lykoi perigenomenoi ekeinōn rhāidiōs kai tēn poimnēn aphylakton ousan diephtheiran.
sentences.l: And the sheep, not foreseeing what was to come, gave them up, and the wolves, having got-the-better-of those easily, destroyed the flock as well, unguarded as it was.
sentences.i: The sheep did not foresee what was coming and surrendered the dogs; and the wolves, having easily made an end of them, destroyed the flock too, now that it had no guard.
sentences.n: μή rather than οὐ with the participle gives it a conditional colour: in that they failed to foresee. τὸ μέλλον is 'the thing about to be', what is coming. ἀφύλακτον οὖσαν is predicative — the flock's being unguarded is the reason it could be destroyed, not merely a description of it.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν πόλεων αἱ τοὺς δημαγωγοὺς ῥᾳδίως προδιδοῦσαι λανθάνουσι καὶ αὐταὶ ταχέως πολεμίοις χειρούμεναι.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn poleōn hai tous dēmagōgous rhāidiōs prodidousai lanthanousi kai autai tacheōs polemiois cheiroumenai.
sentences.l: So too, of cities, those readily betraying their popular leaders escape notice being themselves also quickly brought under the hand of enemies.
sentences.i: So too with cities: those that readily give up their popular leaders are themselves soon subdued by their enemies before they know it.
sentences.n: λανθάνω with a supplementary participle puts the main action in the participle: 'they escape notice being subdued' is English's 'they are subdued before they know it'. τῶν πόλεων is partitive with αἱ … προδιδοῦσαι. χειρόομαι is to bring a thing under one's hand, to subdue, with πολεμίοις the dative of the agent. δημαγωγός is the leader of the people; Attic prose can use it with contempt, but the fable's claim is the plain one, that he is the city's guard-dog.
